# Unity presentation feature fixtures

These independently authored cases use the root feature runner and a copied, isolated native fixture project. They do not modify a live host project. No Unity Editor is configured in the authoring environment: all native compilation/execution remains blocked/not run. Source and simulated report checks must not be reported as native results.

## Executable native cases

Every method is `public static IEnumerator` on `OpenCawUnityPresentationCases`, receives `OpenCawUnityFeatureContext`, and yields only `null`. The runner owns bounded execution, fresh evidence and iterator disposal; `finally` blocks clean up fixture-owned objects and callbacks. Packages are selected and verified before enabling compilation symbols; no case installs or resolves packages.

| Method | Prerequisites/settings | Real effect and limit |
|---|---|---|
| `UIFocus` | Graphics-enabled Editor | Attached UI Toolkit controls acquire modal focus, release underlying controls and restore valid focus; detached control loses ownership. This is Editor-panel evidence, not runtime UIDocument/device QA. |
| `UGUIFocus` | Play Mode; `OPENCAW_UNITY_UGUI` | Actual EventSystem selection moves to a modal and returns; removing one Button listener preserves another. Explicit selection and UnityEvent delivery do not prove physical controller input. |
| `UIFontCoverage` | `OPENCAW_UNITY_TMP`; `tmpFontAsset`, `tmpRequiredCharacters` | Real TMP asset contains each requested Unicode scalar in its primary character table. Does not prove fallback traversal, TextCore shaping, visual readability or dynamic atlas budgets. |
| `LocalizationLifecycle` | Play Mode; `OPENCAW_UNITY_LOCALIZATION`; `localizationLocaleA`, `localizationLocaleB`, `localizationTable`, `localizationEntry`, `localizationExpectedA`, `localizationExpectedB` | Real package initialization, two configured translations, owned-listener removal and late SDK completion rejection. Requires distinct locales and expected strings. |
| `AudioLifecycle` | Play Mode, usable native DSP clock; `audioMixerAsset`, `audioMixerGroupName` | Generated known PCM advances source samples, routes to a real mixer group, stops and resets before reuse. No audibility or CPU-budget claim. |
| `EditorTransactions` | Built-in Editor APIs; runtime probe script | Real Undo/Redo, owned scene save, close/reopen and serialized value preservation. Does not stand in for graph or prefab authoring acceptance. |
| `WebBuild` | Matching Web build module; startup target `WebGL`; `webBuildScene` | Real release BuildPipeline/BuildReport, nonempty runtime files and entry point. Does not certify HTTP headers, browser startup or gameplay. |

The native copied project creates its own imported assets through Unity, not hand-authored binary/YAML fixtures. Setting paths identify real project-local assets. The runner preflight rejects missing or escaping paths. Atlas/tables/font/mixer assets must already be configured in the selected fixture project; tests do not fabricate them to avoid a missing-prerequisite result.

TMP may be supplied by `com.unity.textmeshpro` in older package layouts or bundled in the compatible `com.unity.ugui` package in Unity 6. Verify the actual available `TMPro` assembly/types before defining `OPENCAW_UNITY_TMP`. uGUI requires the actual `UnityEngine.UI`/EventSystems APIs. Localization requires its compatible Addressables/ResourceManager dependencies; the case releases its acquired operation reference without releasing a borrowed table operation.

Audio Play Mode is entered by the root runner with domain reload disabled only in this copied fixture process. That improves test-state ownership; it does not certify the host project's normal reload behavior. The fixture uses low-amplitude PCM but actual audio output can occur. Its DSP configuration note is not a performance measurement. Device listening, spatial review, DSP/streaming CPU and peak-memory profiling remain required separately.

The localization request is deliberately invalidated before its actual SDK completion handler is registered. This reproducibly tests stale-result rejection even when the table is already cached. It does not claim to force an uncached network race. Exercise real cold-load locale changes, remote failures and owned asset handle disposal using the procedure below.

## Supplemental native procedures

Record exact Editor/packages/target, selected stack, asset hashes, expected/observed results, native logs and screenshots/profile captures where relevant. If prerequisites or devices are absent, record blocked/not run; do not replace them with an unconditional pass.

- **Runtime UI and text:** author a real fixture scene through the Editor using the selected uGUI or UIDocument stack. Exercise modal nesting, invalid prior focus, player input isolation, HUD disable/re-enable/respawn, long localized text and viewport/safe-area changes. Capture target-player input and layout evidence. For TMP/TextCore, render required locale samples including combining marks and bidirectional text, grow atlases under load and inspect batches/materials and memory. Test font fallback separately from primary-table coverage.
- **Localization assets:** author two locales, a String Table and an Asset Table with project-owned font/image/audio references. Keep an existing Canvas and independent binding listener. Introduce controlled cold-load delay/failure through a selected local provider, switch A→B→A, disable the screen and replace the asset binding. Verify only current content is applied, owned references release once, surviving listeners still update and the original hierarchy/persistent bindings remain intact. Inspect Addressables resource counts before and after repeated cycles. A deterministic fake provider is simulation evidence unless a real native provider/load is exercised.
- **Editor inspectors:** exercise multi-object edits with mixed values, prefab instance overrides, cancel during a copied multi-asset operation, undo/redo and save/reload. Close and reopen the window, enter/exit Play Mode and reload assemblies; verify owned update/selection subscriptions stop and unrelated subscriptions survive. Build a target player to prove Editor-only code is excluded.
- **Graph Toolkit:** use only an explicitly selected installed version. Resolve the exact graph/node/port API and supported Editor (including the distinct Unity 6.6/6.7 package channels). Through native Editor authoring, create a graph with two nodes and one valid connection, reject an invalid connection, undo/redo, save/reload and compare stable IDs. Convert it to runtime-safe data twice and compare semantic output. Compile a player consuming that data without Editor/Graph Toolkit references. Missing or unsupported package versions block the graph procedure; the basic transaction smoke cannot replace it.
- **Audio:** inspect native mixer paths, snapshots and imported clip load types, then run representative simultaneous effects/music/streaming. Measure peak decoded/streaming memory, voices and Audio Profiler DSP/streaming CPU. Test pause/resume, stolen voices, device configuration change, app suspension and scene teardown. Listen on selected hardware for stereo/spatial behavior, clipping and transitions. Reset all owned pooled source state and prove old completion callbacks cannot stop a new lease.
- **Web player:** build comparable baseline/candidate configurations from the same owned scene set. Serve each locally with the intended compression/MIME/cache headers; inspect real responses, cold/warm loads, console/network failures and content upgrades. Measure encoded bytes, first usable interaction, startup peak memory and gameplay frame-time distributions on representative browsers/devices. Test input, focus, resize, user-gesture audio, suspension and failed-resource UI. Build success alone passes none of these browser assertions.

Never activate paid services, publish, install modules or accept terms to unblock a fixture. Report absent prerequisites with the exact affected check.
